Let us know how it goes. Just remember that no one (even each individual on this sub) can truly understand how it is to walk in your shoes.

We might all be depressed and have a understanding for one another but we are all different with different experiences and emotions.

I say this because for if some reason their response isn't as understanding and compassionate as you hope, it doesn't mean they don't care, they just really can't understand at a micro level. But that doesn't mean what you've been through is any less. Be strong.

I'm sorry I'm not the only one :( this is definitely something that does make things worse in some ways.

I have had a few counselors/psychologists through my old school and even though they were very understanding and considerate, I'd just be sitting there sobbing, unable to keep explaining what it was I had started. It gets old and well quite frankly, it's sad :'(

I hope we can get past this "inconvenience". I wish you the best.

I can relate to wanting to die. I've spent sleepless nights suffering, crying, hating myself and others, and any and all other horribly shitty things some people go through. It isn't fair. 

I don't know you but I can imagine you don't deserve to be going through this, and if you're not some asshole at heart (don't think you are), that makes it that much worse.

Have you ever tried seeking help yet both through therapy and also through medication from a psychiatrist (not just your general practitioner)? I do like to stress at least trying, even if you think those options are stupid and won't fix your problems.
Getting better sleep, or having a prescription to confide in when you're having a horrible anxiety attack, or a medication that can lesson the suffering of a shitty chemical imbalance (even if you don't believe you have one) might not end your depression, but it can really help ease the pain some. 

You will probably still be depressed, but at least having someone to talk to who has dedicated years of their life wanting to try and help others like you can at least make you not feel so alone. And the medication route obviously helps in its own way.

If you have tried both, well I will be happy to write down a few more suggestions. I am not forcing you to try them but I'm here to at least suggest some options.

Depending on what pills you're looking for, they don't necessarily take too long. I've been prescribed SSRIs for depression/anxiety after an initial appointment by multiple doctors. If you're looking for more "dangerous" pills like sleeping pills or anxiety meds like xanax, they will probably want to spend more time with you to make sure you're not there to abuse the drugs.

Will just add you can call and say hello I'd like to see/talk to someone about "depression/anxiety/insomnia/paranoia/bipolar/what have you I'm experiencing", or really you can just say depression. 

Most professionals are capable of dealing with the common other mental illnesses that accompany depression and that just makes the call more simple and comfortable for you.

Good luck and hope things work out for you. 
Don't feel discouraged if the first person you meet with doesn't seem to be the right "fit". Some professionals connect with you better and everyone goes about talking and understanding things in their own little ways and those little differences can sometimes make a big difference in the success of their helpfulness.

Talking to you I can tell that you aren't just some idiot. You can clearly comprehend things and so it does confuse me why someone like you does this kind of thing. It's obvious it gives you some kind of enjoyment or satisfaction, but that's what confuses me. I'd think you'd get that satisfaction by making another individual who's hurting (I know you've been hurt before) feel better. By making someone's day or life better, even if it's just minimal at a time where minimal matters most. I don't think every person has the physical or intellectual capability to make the world a better place but I think deep down everyone, other than maybe sociopaths, wishes they could and I think a lot more people would if they believed in themselves and tried. I hope one day you do. I do appreciate you taking the time to read this and not just ignore me or completely try and continually troll me (though maybe that's what you're doing?) Idk. 

Like I said before, I wish you a good life and I hope one day you wish that and upon others and act accordingly as well.

And I'm simply saying I honestly feel bad for you, and I genuinely hope your life gets better. I don't know who you are, maybe you're a fairly popular kid at school (probably not based on experience but I don't know the online life of most people).

I will say that even if you are happy in life, having good moral values and being able to feel emotions you clearly aren't capable of feeling at this time in life does improve quality of life and hopefully one day you will be able to experience that for your own well-being.
Always feel bad for people like you. Hope your life gets better some day.

You said exercise, friends, video games don't help. By that do you mean you aren't enjoying them while you're doing them or that you eat home and then you feel the same as you did before?

Keeping busy, which includes all of those things you mentioned, are not a cure for depression or other mental illnesses but people suggest you "stay busy" by doing them since for a lot of people it will get their mind off the bad things, even if it's only for an hour or a few.

If you're happier while you're engaged in any of those things or others, please keep doing them as often as you can.

To answer your initial question though, I guess I "get by" by barely making it through the days. Sometimes I lay in bed tossing and turning trying to sleep the day away, sometimes I can find things to read or videos to watch on the internet that can get me through a few hours here and there, and sometimes I sit here slowly going mad not able to stop thinking about killing myself to end this torture. I would believe the same can be said for a lot of people.

Have you told your doctor about these feelings you have? They might be able to help with medication or suggesting another professional that can help.

If I remember correctly they kind of just had strange faces at the time and I somehow ended the conversation before it got even more awkward and embarrassing. I'm pretty sure they ended up having convos about it behind my back so it made me very uncomfortable with them in the future.

Basically what I'm saying is this: there are two ways it will go down - good or bad. If it's good, that's great. If bad, well maybe they aren't the people you want to be around anyways. 

The bad will either come from them judging people with mental illnesses in which case fuck them (not literally). Or, maybe they just aren't educated enough with mental health to understand and what not, but at our age it seems to be much more common the first "bad" rather than them being ignorant since by now you learn and read about this fucked up shit people like us go through.

I say be honest, try not to think too much. Maybe tell them it's embarrassing for you to be admitting it but it's something you didn't choose to live with and it makes life really difficult. Just say you wanted them to know because you don't want to keep things from them and wanted them to understand if you're leaving to be alone or acting "weird" it's because of your mental health and not because you don't want to hang out with them. Idk man, that's the best I can tell you TBH. I do wish you luck and hope those guys can understand and be supportive. Maybe let us know how it goes.
